label: D1 dip after a1 reached S2 (rare a1), growing sharply late in episode
explanation: Raw update gate z of unit 47 saturates near 1 (mean 0.997); nearly all variance beyond timing sits at D1. Its magnitude is set by the previous trial choice x reached state, independent of reward: after a1 that reached S2 (a1 rare transition) z drops (~-0.015 on average, dev weight), after reaching S1 it is slightly higher (+0.003), a2->S2 is neutral. The drop is strongly amplified late in the episode (cubic ramp from trial 80): by trial ~99 the a1->S2 dip reaches ~-0.15 (values down to ~0.77), while late S1 trials sit slightly above and late a2->S2 slightly below the timing baseline, i.e. the late-episode dip in the timing baseline is mostly an a1->S2 effect. Reward, belief (belief_lo adds ~0.01), the trial before and GO/D2 terms add little. Uses only observed quantities (no model value/policy, no future variables); this observed-only explanation reaches test R^2 beyond timing 0.63, above the additive all ceiling 0.34 because of the phase x last-trial x episode-time interaction, so nothing is lost relative to the model-output version (policy decile alone scored 0.11).

issues: The core claims hold up. On test, the original terms score R^2 beyond timing 0.627 (dev 0.632). The residual tables put the D1 dip at about -0.020 after a1 S2 and about +0.004 to +0.006 after S1. GO and D2 residuals are all below 0.0005, so the effect is essentially D1-only. A cubic ramp from trial 80 fits better than the alternatives: power 5 scored 0.605, exp tau=3 scored 0.602, exp tau=2 scored 0.558.

The claim that reward does not matter checks out overall. Early in the episode, a1 S2 r and a1 S2 u differ by only 0.0002. Adding prev_reward*late gives 0.632, and adding a1S2*rewarded*late gives 0.627.

The claim that a2 to S2 is neutral, or only slightly below baseline late in the episode, is too strong. Late a2 to S2 trials whose trial before was an a1 choice dip much more. The term D1*a2S2*(tv('action',-2)==1)*late has weight -0.06 to -0.08 and lifts test R^2 to 0.661. The worst misses are mostly this case, for example after a2 S2c at t97-t99 the actual value is 0.82 against a predicted 0.94-0.95. Within late a2 S2 trials, prev_reward also matters on its own (weight -0.053, test 0.661), but this weight flips sign once the trial-before term is added, so the reward effect there is unstable.
The early a1 S2 dip is not constant: it grows roughly linearly with ep_trial. Adding D1*a1S2*ep_trial/100 (weight -0.017) gives test 0.636.
Belief adds a little: D1*belief_lo*late gives test 0.647, and a2S2*belief_lo*late gives 0.655. That fits the explanation's 'belief adds about 0.01' as an order of magnitude.

No large systematic error class remains. Mean errors by phase are all within 0.001, and by phase x previous trial the largest is 0.002 (D1 after a2 S2 r). About 35% of the variance is still unexplained, but it looks like scattered late-episode noise that varies window to window.
